questions.question: A subsets function calls `result.push(path)` instead of `result.push([...path])`. What happens?
options: It works correctly but uses less memory
Every entry in result points to the same array, which ends up empty after all the pops
It returns only the largest subset
questions.explanation: The shared path array is mutated and restored throughout the search. Pushing the reference stores the same array repeatedly; after backtracking finishes it is empty, so you get a list of empty arrays.

questions.question: In combination sum where each coin may be reused any number of times, what index should the recursive call start from?
questions.explanation: Starting from i lets the same coin be chosen again while still preventing earlier coins (which would create reordered duplicates). i + 1 is for use-each-item-once problems.

questions.question: In N-Queens, which value is the same for every cell on a diagonal running from top-left to bottom-right?
questions.explanation: Moving down-right increases both row and col by 1, so row - col stays constant. row + col is constant on the other (anti) diagonal.

questions.question: What is the typical time complexity of generating all subsets of n elements with backtracking?
questions.explanation: There are 2^n subsets and copying each into the result costs up to O(n), giving O(n * 2^n). Exponential time is unavoidable because the output itself is exponential.
